Particular attention is given to pathogen internalization and viable but non-culturable (VBNC) states, which can compromise the effectiveness of conventional surface decontamination. Chlorine treatments have been reported to achieve reductions of 0.5-6.9 log colony-forming units (CFU) g -1 , organic acids 2.4-3.0 log CFU g -1 and UV-C and cold plasma approximately 3-5 log CFU g -1 , whereas biological agents such as phages and endolysins offer more targeted microbial control. Evidence further indicates that multi-hurdle strategies combining mild organic acid tempering, low-temperature drying and modified atmosphere packaging can provide more consistent microbial control and shelf-life extension than individual interventions. An integrated framework that simultaneously manages enzymatic activity, moisture, temperature, and microbial contamination is therefore critical for improving the safety and stability of sprouted wheat products. Key research gaps include standardized approaches for VBNC detection, long-term storage stability data, regulatory considerations for nanotechnology-based packaging, and scalable and cost-effective preservation technologies. Addressing these challenges could facilitate the safe and sustainable commercialization of sprouted wheat products. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

papers.title: ThermoMutDB 2.0: semiautomated literature curation and structural enrichment of thermostability data for protein mutations.
papers.abstract: Experimental measurements of protein thermodynamic stability are essential for understanding the relationship between protein structure and function, the molecular consequences of mutations, and their potential implications for protein malfunction and disease. However, extracting these data from the literature remains constrained by labor-intensive manual curation. Here, we present ThermoMutDB 2.0, a scalable framework for semiautomated literature curation and systematic structural enrichment. It introduces a major architectural redesign that integrates a large language model with rule-based entity recognition to identify and prioritize publications reporting experimentally measured effects of protein mutations on thermostability, while retaining expert validation as the final curation step. Complementing this literature-processing workflow, ThermoMutDB 2.0 systematically enriches curated mutations with mutant structural models, enabling interactive three-dimensional contextualization of experimentally derived thermodynamic data. Applied to the literature retrieved from January 1976 to the most recent search update in 2026, the pipeline screened 5,934 candidate publications and prioritized 254 for expert review, resulting in the incorporation of 102 articles and 1763 new entries. Rather than representing a simple expansion of database content, ThermoMutDB 2.0 establishes an extensible human-in-the-loop architecture in which automated literature triage, expert curation, and structural modeling operate as an integrated workflow. This redesign provides a sustainable foundation for continuous database maintenance and for linking experimental protein stability measurements with their structural context (available at http://thermomutdb.pathotrack.health/).

papers.title: PlantPAN 5.0: updated database for integrating multiomics evidence and exploring multilayered transcriptional regulatory networks in plants.
papers.abstract: Plant Promoter Analysis Navigator (PlantPAN) 5.0 (https://plantpan.itps.ncku.edu.tw/) is an integrated multiomics resource for investigating plant cis-regulatory elements and transcriptional regulatory networks. This release expands genome annotations and promoter sequences to 240 species and provides 71 040 transcription factor (TF) annotations and 7762 nonredundant binding matrices. Its companion database, PCBase 3.0, substantially expands ChIP-seq data and newly incorporates ATAC-seq, bisulfite-sequencing, and four Hi-C-based chromatin interaction datasets for Arabidopsis thaliana. The new Differential Analysis function enables comparison of TF binding, chromatin accessibility, and DNA methylation across conditions. The redesigned Promoter Analysis interface provides TF family-level statistics, with a Pattern Overview panel integrating TF-binding site (TFBS) densities, plant DNA large language model-predicted open-chromatin regions, CpG-rich regions, and tandem repeats. Two new modules are introduced: (i) Transcriptome Regulatory Analysis and Coexpression, where candidate regulatory TFs and shared cis-elements in gene sets are prioritized through differential expression and coexpression analysis, and (ii) Interaction Topology Analysis for Chromatin and TFs, where chromatin interaction regions are integrated to reveal potentially coregulated genes and their shared TFs and predicted TFBSs. A Dockerized package enables large-scale local promoter analyses, with data privacy. Therefore, PlantPAN 5.0 is a comprehensive framework for discovering plant transcriptional regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Detection of Salmonella Typhimurium using a nanoflower-mediated horseradish peroxidase-linked antibody signal system combined with microfluidic sensors.
papers.abstract: A colorimetric biosensor with a sandwich-type architecture has been successfully constructed for the highly sensitive detection of pathogenic Salmonella typhimurium. Owing to the aptamer-target recognition sensing strategy and the enzyme-mediated signal amplification strategy, the sensing performance is significantly enhanced. In this study, a three-dimensional nanoflower-like structured material was prepared via a facile "one-step synthesis" method. The horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-labeled secondary antibody and the Salmonella typhimurium-specific aptamer were incorporated as organic components into the organic-inorganic nanocomposite, serving as the signal label of the colorimetric biosensor. In the presence of H₂O₂, the HRP-labeled antibody oxidizes the colorless substrate TMB to a colored product, thereby enabling simultaneous signal amplification and colorimetric detection. Furthermore, the integration with a microfluidic device renders the operation more convenient and straightforward. Under the optimal experimental conditions, the proposed biosensor exhibited excellent detection performance, with a linear range of 10²~10⁷ CFU/mL and a detection limit as low as 1.41 CFU/ml. It also possessed good selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. In summary, leveraging its unique structural advantages, this biosensor holds broad application prospects and research value in the field of pathogen detection and on-site rapid screening.

papers.title: [A case of Mowat-Wilson syndrome due to a de novo c.3515del frameshift variant of ZEB2 gene].
papers.abstract: To explore the genetic etiology of a fetus with Mowat-Wilson syndrome (MWS) due to a novel de novo heterozygous frameshift variant of ZEB2 gene. A pedigree presenting at the Affiliated Women and Children's Hospital of Ningbo University in February 2024 was enrolled. Clinical data were retrospectively analyzed. Amniotic fluid samples of the fetus and peripheral blood samples of the couple were collected for trio-whole exome sequencing (Trio-WES). Candidate variant was verified by Sanger sequencing. The pathogenicity of the candidate variant was assessed based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG). Postnatal follow-up was performed, and the pathogenicity of the variant was re-assessed by incorporating newly acquired phenotypic features. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: EC2023-094). Prenatal ultrasonography at 20 +2 weeks of gestation identified ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta and polyhydramnios. Trio-WES revealed that the fetus has harbored a novel c.3515del (p.Met1172ArgfsTer69) heterozygous frameshift variant of the ZEB2 gene. Sanger sequencing confirmed that neither parent has carried the same variant. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the variant was initially classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) based on PVS1_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PS2_Supporting criteria. After birth, the infant exhibited typical MWS features including hypertelorism, low-hanging columella, neck hypotonia, cerebral hypoplasia, corpus callosum agenesis, and abnormal earlobe morphology. Growth delay, feeding difficulties, and motor delay were observed at 4-month follow-up. Combined with postnatal phenotypic data, the variant was re-classified as likely pathogenic (LP) based on PVS1_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PS2_Moderate+PP4_Supporting criteria. The newly identified ZEB2 c.3515del represents a likely pathogenic variant, which expanded the mutational spectrum of the ZEB2 gene. Longitudinal prenatal-to-postnatal phenotypic integration is critical for re-assessing VUS in MWS patients and providing evidence-based references for prenatal genetic diagnosis and genetic counseling of similar cases.

papers.title: [Genetic analysis and prenatal diagnosis for a Chinese pedigree affected with X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia due to variant of EDA gene].
papers.abstract: To explore molecular basis for a Chinese pedigree affected with X-linked hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia (XLHED). A Chinese pedigree presenting at the Northwest Women's and Children's Hospital in October 2023 was enrolled in this study. Clinical data were retrospectively analyzed. Peripheral blood samples were collected from the proband and his family members for genomic DNA extraction. Whole exome sequencing (WES) was carried out to screen for candidate pathogenic variants. Sanger sequencing was used to validate these variants within the pedigree, followed by pathogenicity assessment of the candidate variants. Chorionic villus sampling was conducted during the first trimester for prenatal diagnosis in two pregnant relatives (the proband's mother and maternal aunt). This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: 2024-027). The proband, a 7-year-old boy, exhibited classic features of XLHED including hypodontia and sparse hair. Genetic analysis identified a hemizygous c.572_573insC (p.Gly192Argfs*48) frameshift variant in exon 4 of the EDA gene. Both the proband's mother and maternal aunt were heterozygous for this variant but remained asymptomatic. Segregation analysis traced the variant to the proband's maternal grandfather, who displayed a phenotype similar to that of the proband. Based on the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, the variant was classified as pathogenic (PVS1+PP4+PM2_Supporting). The variant was unreported previously. Subsequent chorionic villus sampling confirmed that neither fetus had carried the same variant, and postnatal follow-up revealed normal phenotypes in both infants. The c.572_573insC (p.Gly192Argfs*48) variant of the EDA gene probably underlay the XLHED in this pedigree. Above finding has expanded the mutational spectrum of the EDA gene and facilitated the prenatal management. The lack of clinical expression in female heterozygous carriers underscores the importance of accurate risk assessment in genetic counseling for pedigrees affected with XLHED.

papers.title: [Genetic analysis of a child with Frontometaphyseal dysplasia 1 due to variant of FLNA gene and literature review].
papers.abstract: To explore the clinical characteristics and genetic etiology of a child with Frontometaphyseal dysplasia 1 (FMD1) due to variant of FLNA gene. A child who presented at the Department of Endocrinology, the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University in July 2025 with a 6-year history of prominent supraorbital ridges was selected as study subject. Clinical data of the child were collected. Peripheral venous blood samples were collected from the child and his parents for the extraction of genomic DNA. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) was carried out, and candidate variant was validated by Sanger sequencing. Pathogenicity of the variant was rated based on guidelines from the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG). Structure of the mutant protein was predicted using AlphaFold and PyMOL software. Literature retrieval was performed using Chinese and English keywords "FLNA gene" and "frontometaphyseal dysplasia". The clinical manifestations and inheritance patterns of previously reported cases with the variant were analyzed. This study was approved by the Ethics Committee of the hospital (Ethics No.: 25971). The child exhibited multiple skeletal deformities including prominent supraorbital ridges, micrognathia, hearing loss, scoliosis, long bone curvature, broad and flat deformities of the thumbs and great toes, and joint contractures. Additionally, he was complicated with congenital urinary tract obstruction. WES revealed that he has harbored a hemizygous missense variant c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) in exon 22 of the FLNA gene, which showed a strong correlation with his clinical phenotype. Sanger sequencing confirmed this variant to be de novo in origin. Based on the ACMG guidelines, the FLNA c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) variant was classified as pathogenic (PS4_Moderate+PM2_Supporting+PM6+PP1_Strong+PP2+PP3). Protein structural modeling suggested that this variant could reduce local hydrogen bonds, which may weaken local anchoring force. Literature review has retrieved 8 articles (1 in Chinese) related to FMD1 due to the FLNA c.3557C>T variant. Together with the present case, a total of 14 patients (13 males and 1 female) were included. All patients showed obvious supraorbital hyperplasia (100.0%). Other common manifestations included wrist/distal joint contracture (14 cases), micrognathia (10 cases), scoliosis (10 cases), and spatulate thumbs/toes (9 cases). Other manifestations included hearing loss (8 cases), permanent tooth agenesis (8 cases), long bone bowing (8 cases), hypertelorism (8 cases). Urinary tract malformations (3 cases) and cardiovascular malformations (2 cases) were relatively rare. Analysis of the inheritance pattern showed that 2 of the 14 patients carried de novo variants, and the remaining 12 patients were from 9 families, with their mothers as heterozygous carriers (one mosaic). This study has diagnosed a child with FMD1 due to a hemizygous c.3557C>T (p.Ser1186Leu) missense variant of the FLNA gene, which expanded the mutational spectrum of FMD1.

papers.title: Mathematical modeling in mRNA therapeutics: toward a pathway to individualized treatment protocols.
papers.abstract: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) therapeutics represent a transformative pharmacological paradigm where the delivery vehicle, genetic payload, and expressed protein form a tightly coupled system. This multicomponent structure introduces nonlinear, multiscale dynamics that challenge traditional pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic frameworks, making quantitative modeling essential. This review provides a structured biological framework for mRNA-LNP therapeutics, detailing the key processes governing delivery, endosomal escape, mRNA stability, and translation, and highlighting their associated temporal and spatial scales, providing the key aspects to consider for modeling. Building on this foundation, we summarize mathematical modeling approaches, including pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK), and quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) models, used to represent these mechanisms. The literature was surveyed to identify representative preclinical and translational studies, focusing on model structure, assumptions, and their use in human projection and dose optimization. Mathematical models are critical to interpret and predict mRNA therapeutic behavior, yet challenges remain in parameter identifiability, data availability, and model standardization. Future advances will depend on biologically grounded modeling frameworks, improved integration of mechanistic insight with quantitative approaches, and tighter coupling between experimental design and model development. These developments will support species translation and enable precision medicine applications.

papers.title: The spatiotemporal ecosystem of gallbladder cancer: From inflamed areas to invasive margins - Integrating biomechanical injury, the bile microenvironment, precursor lineages, and spatial niches.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) is usually described as the end point of chronic cholelithiasis-associated inflammation, and yet this linear formulation does not explain why only a small fraction of people with gallstones develop cancer, why histologically similar precursor lesions follow different evolutionary routes, or why invasion preferentially advances through anatomically and immunologically distinct interfaces. We propose a spatiotemporal ecosystem model that links five domains: gallstones and reflux as precipitating conditions; bile as a chemically active habitat; resident or transient microorganisms as context-dependent modifiers; metaplastic, biliary intraepithelial and intracholecystic precursor lineages as alternative epithelial trajectories; and stromal-immune niches that select for invasive phenotypes. Evidence from epidemiology, pathology, genomics, organoid and animal models, single-cell sequencing, and spatial profiling is integrated while preserving distinctions between association, mechanism, and clinical prediction. The strongest causal chain currently links prolonged mechanical or reflux injury with cycles of epithelial loss and repair, metaplastic or dysplastic changes, and acquisition of driver alterations. Microbial findings are biologically plausible and increasingly supported by functional Salmonella studies, but most human biliary microbiome datasets remain small and vulnerable to low-biomass contamination and treatment-related confounding. Precursor studies substantiate the existence of both BilIN progression in affected areas and alternative polypoid or BilIN-independent routes, arguing against a single obligatory sequence. Recent single-cell and spatial studies have identified organized, region-specific interactions among malignant epithelial states, macrophages, exhausted CD8 T cells, neutrophils, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, hepatocytes, and nerves at invasive margins. Liver-facing, serosal, perineural, lymphovascular, and nodal interfaces should not be assumed to share one ecology. These data shift the central question from which mutation is present to where a clone resides, which neighboring cells sustain it, and when the niche becomes permissive. The model suggests testable priorities: longitudinal sampling of high-risk gallbladders, paired bile-mucosa profiling with rigorous controls, lineage-resolved multi-section spatial analysis, and boundary-aware biomarkers validated in prospective cohorts.

papers.title: Genetic and laboratory predictors of bleeding severity in FVII deficiency: insights from the PRO-RBDD and EN-RBD databases.
papers.abstract: Factor VII deficiency (FVIID) is among the most common rare bleeding disorders. The ability of FVII coagulant activity (FVII:C) levels and genetic variants to predict clinical outcomes remain limited. We evaluated the discriminative performance of FVII:C levels, genotype-phenotype associations, and the accuracy of in silico tools in identifying pathogenic variants. In total, 422 patients from 3 international registries were analyzed. Overall, 61% experienced bleeding, predominantly spontaneous (73%); 20% had grade I, 27% had grade II, and 14% had grade III bleeding. Lower FVII:C levels showed a moderate inverse correlation with bleeding scores and were more common in individuals with spontaneous bleeding (r = -0.49; P< .0001). FVII:C levels showed moderate discrimination for asymptomatic status (area under the curve [AUC], 0.72) and strong discrimination for grade III bleeding (AUC, 0.84). Cutoffs of ≥19 IU/dLand <11 IU/dL identified asymptomatic individuals and those with grade III bleeding. We identified 90 variants, including 10 novel; 60% were missense, and 63% localized to the serine protease domain. According to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria, 86% were pathogenic/likely pathogenic. The sensitivity of in silico tools was 96%, 85%, and 60% for REVEL, CADD, and AlphaMissense. Severe deficiency was more common in homozygous individuals (90%), whereas heterozygous individuals predominantly exhibited mild/moderate deficiency (92%). Consistently, bleeding phenotypes were frequent in individuals with homozygous/compound heterozygous variants, whereas most heterozygous variants were asymptomatic (71%). Overall, FVII:C levels moderately stratify bleeding severity. Homozygous/compound heterozygous variants are associated with lower FVII:C levels and more severe bleeding, whereas heterozygous variants are mostly asymptomatic. Among in silico tools, REVEL demonstrated the highest sensitivity.

papers.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
papers.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

papers.title: Functional genomics reveals mediators of beta cell survival in ER stress and type 2 diabetes risk
papers.abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in pancreatic beta cells contributes to impaired function and type 2 diabetes (T2D). In this study we performed genome-wide perturbation screens and genomic profiling in beta cells to identify novel mediators of ER stress responses and diabetes risk. We defined gene regulatory networks in beta cells and identified specific beta cell networks enriched for T2D risk variants with altered expression in ER stress. We performed a loss-of-function CRISPR screen for survival under ER stress in EndoC-bH1 cells, which identified 167 pro-survival and 47 pro-death genes involved in processes related to insulin secretion, mitochondrial transport and protein ubiquitination. Beta cell survival genes collectively had limited genomic change in stress yet showed significant, independent enrichment for T2D risk variants, including novel T2D candidate gene DTNB which we validated protects against beta cell death during stress. Overall, our results revealed mediators of ER stress responses in beta cells and identified novel therapeutic targets to preserve beta cells in diabetes pathogenesis.

papers.title: ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA): An Agentic Framework for Feature Discovery and Cross Site Generalization in Autism fMRI Classification
papers.abstract: Classifiers of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) from resting state functional MRI rarely generalize across sites, and many reported accuracies are inflated by data leakage.We show that an agentic artificial intelligence framework, ASD Neuro Agentic (ANA), whose language model agents propose features from the literature and researcher input while fixed tools perform every calculation, can search auditably for site independent classifiers while controlling the leakage. In 1,028 participants from 17 ABIDE I centers, ANA tested 71 pipelines and selected a ComBat harmonized ensemble of tangent space connectivity models from six parcellations and 98 public connectivity derivatives. In leave one center out testing, the ensemble reached an area under the curve of 0.814 (95% CI, 0.773 to 0.841), outperforming ASD DiagNet and ASD SAENet. Predictive connectivity was mainly reduced in ASD. Agentic AI offers a systematic and efficient approach to exploring, evaluating, and identifying pipelines as model selection grows complex.

papers.title: pLM-bVAE: protein language model-enhanced binary representation improves quantum annealing-based protein sequence design
papers.abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) has been explored as an approach for protein design in vast combinatorial sequence spaces. Applying QA to protein sequence design requires amino acid sequences to be encoded as binary vectors, and optimized vectors to be decoded back into amino acid sequences. Thus, both the quality of binary encoding and sequence reconstruction accuracy are important for effective QA-based optimization. Binary variational autoencoder (bVAE) has been used to map protein sequences to binary representations in QA-based protein sequence design. However, bVAE was originally developed for natural language modeling, and its suitability for proteins has not been systematically evaluated. Here, we present pLM-bVAE, which incorporates protein representations derived from a pretrained protein language model (pLM) into the original bVAE model. In computational experiments on three public protein variant datasets, pLM-bVAE showed higher sequence reconstruction accuracy and binary encoding performance than bVAE. Moreover, we incorporated pLM-bVAE into a QA-based protein sequence design framework. Across all three datasets, pLM-bVAE generated more high-scoring sequences with greater sequence dissimilarity from the training and validation data than bVAE. Our results demonstrate that pLM-bVAE provides an effective binary representation for improving QA-based protein sequence design. Availability The source code used in this manuscript is available at https://github.com/hueda8/pLM-bVAE.

papers.title: CPDD: Adapting an autoregressive DNA language model for bidirectional phage genome modeling
papers.abstract: Autoregressive DNA language models generate sequences ef[fi]ciently from left to right, but many genome-analysis and sequence-editing problems are naturally conditioned on both [fl]anks. We introduce CreatiPhage, a 144.5M-parameter autoregressive DNA language model for bacteriophages, and its diffusion extension, CreatiPhage Diffusion DNA-LM (CPDD). CPDD is a 147.5M-parameter bidirectional discrete diffusion model initialized from the six-epoch CreatiPhage checkpoint. CPDD retains the pretrained Transformer, block attention residuals, and Engram conditional memory, while introducing non-causal attention, a MASK-aware base-5 Engram, centered depthwise convolution, and position-aligned nucleotide readout. Training combines masked and GIDD-style uniformly substituted bases with nucleotide- and amino-acid-level losses over a 10 kb, 32 kb, and whole-source context curriculum. On a screened panel of 522 phage CDSs, CPDD achieves higher random-mask restoration accuracy than a comparable diffusion model and performs well above codon-level references. In a mixed-corruption test, it restores 42.4% of visible incorrect bases. Frozen CPDD representations also support infA [fi]tness prediction and seven-class phage virion protein subtype classi[fi]cation. Controlled evaluations further characterize how restoration depends on visible context and identify opportunities to improve longer-range sequence recovery. Together, these results support scaffold-conditioned sequence modeling as a step towards modular design of phage genomes.

papers.title: LingoCell interprets gene perturbations through natural language and tissue niches
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models are general tools for resolving cell identities and disease states, but struggle to interpret changes in expression magnitude in biological language, to transfer to sparse spatial measurements, and to explain cellular niches. We introduce LingoCell, a foundation model connecting single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. It aligns cell representations with language while keeping gene expression editable, supporting cell annotation, cross-batch integration, description generation, and disease-language readouts of single-gene and combinatorial in silico perturbations. Extended to tissues, it annotates cells without single-cell references, learns identity-conditioned niche embeddings, and performs spatial in silico perturbation by replacing and editing neighbor expression. In lung adenocarcinoma, LingoCell revealed synergistic disease responses to jointly weakening alveolar differentiation programs and strengthening malignant programs. In colorectal cancer, it revealed different programs conveyed by the same fibroblast state to T cells, macrophages, and tumor cells. LingoCell provides a unified framework for prioritizing target combinations and stromal intervention programs.

papers.title: Batch, Prefetch, Skip, Orient, Squeeze: Faster, Smaller k-mer dictionaries via the Spectral Burrows-Wheeler transform
papers.abstract: Looking up k-mers in an index is a core operation in genomics, underlying read mapping, metagenomic classification, and many other tasks. Queries are often streaming: the k-mers come from a longer sequence such as a sequencing read, and consecutive k-mers overlap. The fastest index for such queries is currently the hashing-based SSHash; indexes based on the spectral Burrows-Wheeler transform (SBWT) are competitive in space but slower. We show how to make SBWT indexes both faster and smaller. First, we process queries in small batches and prefetch the memory each will need next, hiding the latency of the dependent random accesses that dominate a lookup; together with a new rank structure that reads one cache line per query, this makes k-mer lookups about seven times faster than unbatched SBWT search. Second, we extend batching to streaming search and show that one failed lookup can rule out many k-mers of a read at once, which removes the need for the longest common suffix array. Third, we build an SBWT that stores only one orientation of each k-mer, thereby halving its size, with a modified search that exploits how rarely the orientation changes along a read. Finally, we adapt a compact subset rank structure to batched search. On the collections of the SSHash benchmark, and on two collections up to 15 times larger, our fastest index answers streaming queries for 31-mers faster than SSHash on every read set, by up to 4.9 times, using 12 bits per canonical k-mer against SSHash's 7.4-11.1. We also show that a 6.1-bit index is still faster than SSHash on most read sets, and that our smallest index needs about 4 bits per canonical k-mer. Unlike that of SSHash, the space of our indexes barely varies across collections. Our code is available at https://github.com/anadis504/sbwt-squeeze-rs.

papers.title: DecoyOpt: A two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate and efficient EC number prediction is essential for elucidating the catalytic roles of enzymes. Although similarity-based and deep learning-based approaches have advanced this task, they often fail to distinguish active enzymes from closely related decoys inactivated by local functional-site mutations, leading to high false-positive rates (FPRs). We propose DecoyOpt, a two-stage pipeline for decoy-aware enzyme discrimination and EC number prediction. Specifically, we generated putatively inactive functional-site decoys using ESM3 and evaluated 16 protein language models across three splits. An MLP trained with classification and ranking losses distinguishes enzymes from unannotated proteins and decoys before a contrastive learning model assigns EC numbers to predicted enzymes. On the most stringent GraphPart 40% split, DecoyOpt achieves an MCC of 0.899 and a D0 decoy FPR of 6.17%, outperforming retrained baselines. Across all splits, it outperforms these baselines in EC number prediction on the full test set while maintaining performance close to CLEAN on the enzyme subset. It also correctly annotates all four wild-type enzymes and rejects all eight inactive or nearly inactive variants. We believe that DecoyOpt has potential for annotating uncharacterized proteins and their variants, with applications in genomics, synthetic biology, and biocatalysis.

papers.title: Cross-state representation learning enables prospective discovery of dynamic protein allosteric sites
papers.abstract: Allosteric regulation offers multifunctional induction in therapeutic interventions, yet conformational plasticity hinders computational identification of allosteric sites. Machine learning models rely on static holo (ligand-bound) structures, generalizing poorly to apo or substrate-bound states where binding pockets are transient or cryptic. We present AsBench2, a cross-state site-recognition benchmark, and AllositeUltra, a deep learning framework integrating multimodal protein representations (combining structure-aware language models with physical dynamics) and residue-guided candidate supplementation, effectively decoupling site detection from static pocket geometry. AllositeUltra demonstrates superior generalization, achieving Top-3 site recovery rates of 65.2% and 70.6% on apo and substrate-bound structures, respectively, representing relative improvements of 36.4% and approximately 50% over the best-performing baselines. Prospective application to MAGI2 identifies a previously unrecognized interdomain allosteric pocket, validated at atomic resolution through small-molecule screening and X-ray crystallography. Proteome-wide application yields a high-confidence atlas of targetable allosteric sites, bridging the gap between structural representation learning and prospective AI-driven drug discovery.

papers.title: EMtrace: offline nanopore metagenomics on a laptop for rapid viral diagnostics, genome recovery and 16S profiling
papers.abstract: Nanopore sequencers produce reads within minutes, but metagenomic analysis remains challenging where internet access is limited, data are sensitive or computing resources are modest. EMtrace is an offline pipeline that runs on a laptop during sequencing: it classifies MinKNOW reads, estimates taxon abundance by expectation-maximization (EM) and assembles reference-based consensus genomes. We benchmarked it against five virome and four 16S rRNA tools on simulated, mock-community and clinical data. On field isolates and 16 SARS-CoV-2 clinical samples, EMtrace had the highest species-level F1 score (1.00 and 0.97) and one false-positive species, against 3-7 for the comparators. It recovered divergent viruses as completely as ViMOP, and low-titre field libraries more completely, at [≥]99.7% identity. In replayed runs, it identified the target virus in the first 4,000-read batch (5-13 min). With a shared 16S reference, EMtrace reported two to three times fewer false-positive species than Emu.

papers.title: Uncovering cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial omics
papers.abstract: Individual cells simultaneously encode multiple biological signals in their gene expression profiles, including spatial position, circadian phase, and disease state. These signals can be entangled in complex ways, including circadian patterns that vary along disease progression and cell cycle dynamics that shift along developmental trajectories. While methods to disentangle such signals have been recently developed, characterizing the interaction itself between multicellular signals along with its effects on tissue function, localizing cellular subpopulations which exhibit signal interactions, and identifying potential candidate genes which drive such interactions, all remain major challenges. We present CRISP which characterizes signal interactions in single-cell gene expression data based on the correspondence between the multiple, probabilistic signal-specific projections of the data. Across simulations with tunable couplings and four single-cell and spatial transcriptomic datasets, CRISP recovers diverse biological signal interactions and localizes them to informative cellular subpopulations and groups of associated genes; CRISP distinguishes healthy from fibrotic liver samples and localizes the loss of zonation-position coupling to individual fibrotic hepatocytes, resolves the asymmetric coupling of TGF-{beta} response, EMT, and cell-cycle phase to specific cell subpopulations, and flags transcriptionally delayed hepatocytes in Plasmodium liver infection. Beyond quantifying and localizing signal interactions, CRISP can refine existing labels, uncover continuous cellular transitions and reveal condition-associated genes.

papers.title: Language-guided domain adaptation improves protein sequence representations for antimicrobial resistance analysis
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), particularly antibiotic resistance in bacterial pathogens, complicates infectious disease management. Because bacterial resistance is often mediated by protein functions, including antibiotic inactivation and efflux, protein sequence analysis provides a molecular basis for digital AMR surveillance and therapeutic intervention. We developed BacLLM, a language guided protein representation framework that integrates annotation-derived functional knowledge into protein language model representations for AMR analysis in WHO priority bacterial pathogens. Through sequence enhancement, semantic enrichment of UniProt annotations, and cross modal contrastive learning, BacLLM transfers LLM encoded annotation priors into the sequence encoder. Compared with baselines, BacLLM provided more informative representations for resistance-gene identification and mechanism prediction, captured resistance associated mutational signals at single-residue resolution, and preserved taxonomic relationships not reflected by phenotype based clinical groupings. Moreover, BacLLM recovered resistance associated functional organization within a TolC-centered protein association network, prioritizing proteins with low sequence identity to TolC but predicted structural similarity to TolC. Extending from AMR characterization to therapeutic prioritization, BacLLM also improved strain-level phage host matching for phage therapy candidate prioritization. Together, these findings establish BacLLM as a protein representation framework supporting AMR surveillance, functional characterization, and therapeutic candidate prioritization.

papers.title: Assessing the Capacity of Genomic Language Models to Generate Informative Embeddings of Viral Genome Fragments
papers.abstract: Genomic language models (gLMs) trained on large volumes of nucleotide sequences are becoming an alternative to classical methods in metagenomic analysis, particularly for studying genomic "dark matter". In this work, we investigate the ability of four gLMs (DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM, and Evo2-7B) to generate taxonomically informative vector representations of short viral genome fragments. We constructed a balanced reference dataset of viruses based on the ICTV Virus Metadata Resource and compared the representations generated by gLMs with conventional k-mer profiles and MinHash sketches using clustering and neighborhood-based metrics (adjusted Rand index (ARI), precision@k, and CROSS precision@k). On the reference dataset, three of the four gLMs outperformed the 4-mer profile in terms of ARI and precision@5 under the same evaluation protocol. The best performance was generally achieved by intermediate model layers. Conventional k-mer profiles consistently outperformed MinHash sketches. We further evaluated the methods on two viral orders (egoviruses and mriyaviruses) absent from the reference dataset, with model layers and k-mer lengths selected exclusively on the reference dataset. DNABERT-S showed the most consistently strong performance across these two orders, ranking first on mriyaviruses and second on egoviruses, while k-mer profiles with Jensen-Shannon distance remained competitive. We also observed the consistency of representations between forward fragments and their reverse complements. Overall, the best-performing gLMs surpassed conventional baselines, although their advantage depended on the dataset and evaluation metric. The consistently strong performance of DNABERT-S suggests a potential benefit of contrastive fine-tuning and indicates that larger models are not necessarily more effective for generating taxonomically informative representations.

papers.title: An auditable harness for biomolecular dynamics simulations by AI agents
papers.abstract: AI agents now generate biological hypotheses faster than they can be tested. Hypotheses stated at the atomic level can be examined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. For new questions without a reference, trust in an agent-run simulation rests on a tool-written process record, not the agent's account. Existing MD agents leave this record to the language model. Here we present MDClaw, a harness whose validating tools and directed acyclic graph (DAG) check stages before execution and record every simulation stage. On MDDataBench, which grades outputs against deposited simulations, four open-weight models with MDClaw passed all three runs on 81-100% of 31 test systems. The DAG complements this outcome check. An ablation without the DAG revealed 11 successful runs that had skipped minimization or equilibration, or simulated a different structure. MDClaw carried questions from human and AI scientists through simulation to trajectories traceable to their inputs and settings.

papers.title: Beyond Sequence and Structure: Pretraining PLMs on Continuous Biophysical Fields
papers.abstract: We introduce the Biophysical Transformer, a protein language model that adds continuous biophysical fields as a third pretraining signal beside sequence and structure. A Poisson-Boltzmann solver computes the electrostatic potential around each three-residue token, and the model learns to predict it from sequence alone. A rotationally invariant spherical-harmonic descriptor serves as the loss target, eliminating the need for frame alignment during training and for coordinates at inference. Against a matched, one-flag control on the FLIP Meltome thermostability benchmark, the field objective raises Spearman correlation on every trained head of both human splits.The gain on human survives residualizing dipeptide composition under two architecturally different readouts and survives removing the test proteins that overlap the pretraining corpus. No effect survives on the organism-mixed split. At 1.1M parameters, both the Biophysical Transformer and its sequence-only control exceed FLIP's one-hot CNN and untrained-ESM baselines on every split. All results rest on a single pretraining run per arm,and the current design does not separate field content from generic regularization.

papers.title: BryoCAD: Extending Plant DNA Foundation Models Beyond Flowering Plants
papers.abstract: Bryophytes exhibit diverse genome architectures and gene repertoires, yet their functional interpretation remains constrained by incomplete genomic annotations and limited experimental resources. Although DNA foundation models offer promising solutions, their applicability to evolutionarily divergent bryophytes remains largely unexplored. Here, we introduce BryoCAD, a DNA language model developed through continued pre-training of the angiosperm-specific PlantCAD2 model on 17 bryophyte genomes spanning hornworts, liverworts, and mosses. Across three representative bryophyte genomes and four gene-boundary motif recovery tasks, BryoCAD-Small improved mean zero-shot accuracy from 45.7% to 57.0%, a 24.8% relative increase over PlantCAD2-Small, while the over 200-fold larger Evo2-20B achieved a mean accuracy of only 39.3%. Remarkably, BryoCAD-Small outperformed PlantCAD2-Large in 11 of 12 motif-recovery comparisons across the three bryophytes, highlighting the benefits of lineage-specific adaptation over model scaling alone. These improvements extended to all six tested algal species, increasing mean accuracy from 26.3% to 37.5%, although performance varied across ferns and gymnosperms. BryoCAD also enhanced gene structure annotation: replacing PlantCAD2-Small with BryoCAD-Small increased transcript-level F1 scores from 0.578 to 0.625 in Marchantia polymorpha and from 0.485 to 0.530 in Physcomitrium patens. Together, our findings demonstrate that lineage-specific continued pre-training enhances genomic sequence interpretation and gene annotation across bryophytes, providing a transferable framework for extending DNA foundation models to evolutionarily diverse, understudied plant lineages.

papers.title: RNA Small-Molecule Binding-Site Prediction by Integrating RNA Language Models and Structural Geometry
papers.abstract: RNAs are emerging as promising therapeutic targets, and small-molecule binding can modulate their structure and function, creating opportunities for therapeutic development. Accurate identification of RNA small-molecule binding sites is therefore important for understanding RNA-ligand interactions and facilitating RNA-targeted drug discovery. However, the structural complexity of RNA and the limited availability of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes pose challenges for computational binding-site prediction. In this study, we propose RSMBind, a graph attention-based deep learning framework for nucleotide-level prediction of RNA-small molecule binding sites. The model integrates geometric descriptors of the local three-dimensional environment with pretrained RNA language model embeddings to capture complementary structural and sequence information. We investigate three pretrained RNA language models RNA-BERT, ERNIE-RNA and RNA-FM and assess the contributions of sequence representations and geometric features through feature-level ablation experiments. The model is developed using the TR60 and HARIBOSS datasets and evaluated on four independent benchmark datasets: RB9, TE18, TL12 and JL10. RSMBind achieves the highest MCC among the compared methods on three of the four benchmarks, with relative improvements of 17.1% on RB9, 7.2% on TL12 and 16.0% on JL10 over the best previously reported results, while achieving competitive performance on TE18. Furthermore, RSMBind retains predictive capability when using only pretrained RNA language model embeddings, highlighting their potential utility when explicit tertiary structural features are unavailable. Structural analysis indicates differences in prediction performance across RNA structural regions, with loop-associated binding sites generally being captured more effectively than those embedded within stem regions. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of selected RNA-ligand complexes provide insights into the relationship between predicted binding probabilities and dynamic ligand proximity, further highlighting the role of conformational dynamics in evaluating structure-based predictions. The source code is available at [ https://github.com/sharma-nandita/RSMBind].

papers.title: Longitudinal CCR2 PET Imaging Tracks Early Inflammatory Monocyte and Macrophage Infiltration in Experimental Arthritis
papers.abstract: Objective. Recruitment of C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2+) inflammatory monocytes and macrophages represent an early event in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis that cannot be tracked noninvasively with existing imaging modalities. We evaluated longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) to track and quantify CCR2 cell recruitment in experimental inflammatory arthritis. Methods. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT imaging was performed in K/BXN serum transfer arthritis (STA) mice. Imaging findings were validated using biodistribution, autoradiography, histopathology, immunofluorescence, microCT, cytokine profiling, clinical assessment, and pain-related behavioral testing. Results. Joint Ga-DOTA-ECL1i uptake increased during the acute arthritis and declined with disease resolution. Increased tracer signal localized to inflamed joints, coinciding with CCR2 monocyte and macrophage infiltration, synovial inflammation, cartilage damage, local CCL2 elevation, and mechanical allodynia. PET uptake correlated with ankle swelling, clinical disease severity, pain, and paw CCL2 levels, with peak tracer signal preceding progressive structural bone remodeling. Conclusion. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT enables noninvasive visualization and quantification of early CCR2 monocyte and macrophage recruitment, establishing CCR2 PET imaging as a mechanism-based molecular platform for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring in inflammatory arthritis.

papers.title: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
papers.abstract: Background: Proper adoption of AI in emergency medicine necessitate thorough and rigorous appraisal. Classic benchmarks, which rely heavily on basic question-and-answer formats, though dominating the benchmarking field of LLM usage in medicine, have proven inadequate in assessing the full spectrum of skills incumbent upon an agent in healthcare. Methods: We propose an intricate benchmarking scheme in which the skill set required of an emergency physician is tested and quantified. Our benchmarking structure is 3-fold: skills such as history taking, diagnostic accuracy, treatment plan, and empathy are evaluated by an emergency medicine expert, while the same expertise is scored by an intern from the perspective of a patient, through what we call a simulated emergency room visit. A comprehensive written examination is also utilized to measure general emergency medicine knowledge. Results: Eight LLMs were benchmarked against each other and in contrast to nine emergency medical doctors. Our findings indicate that the AI models significantly outperformed human physicians across several key domains, including history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment planning. Furthermore, the models demonstrated superior performance in comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy. When comparing AI models against each other, performance advantages were marginal during simulated emergency room visits and were mostly pronounced during the written examination. Conclusion: AI models demonstrate a clear advantage over human physicians across a diverse range of emergency medicine competencies. The proposed benchmarking scheme provides a comprehensive metric for a thorough evaluation of medical skill set, furthering validation, adaptation, and utilization of AI in emergency medicine.

papers.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients
papers.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Methods: Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45 or CD45CD11b cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. Results: We performed CITE-seq analysis on ~38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+ and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. Conclusions: These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

papers.title: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
papers.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet whether external eye photographs carry phenotypic information about posterior segment disease remains unclear, and methods to mitigate demographic disparities in such models are largely unexplored. We developed and evaluated deep learning and vision-language models for binary classification of vision-threatening DR (VTDR), advanced AMD, and glaucoma using 40,687 external eye photographs from 9,878 patients at Massachusetts Eye and Ear. Convolutional networks (WResNet, EfficientNet), a vision transformer (ViT), and a fine-tuned vision-language model (LLaVA) were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with fairness across sex, race, and ethnicity quantified by the equity-scaled AUC (ES-AUC). Five fairness-training strategies were applied to the best models. LLaVA achieved the highest baseline AUC for VTDR (85.4%, comparable to ViT 82.6%); advanced AMD was similar across architectures (EfficientNet 86.3%; LLaVA 84.8%; ViT 84.7%), whereas glaucoma was substantially worse (67-74%). Fairness training improved VTDR and AMD AUCs to 86.3% and 85.9% while partially mitigating demographic disparities. In summary, although AI models that rely on external eye photography to detect posterior segment disease may not yet be suitable for clinical deployment, the fairness methods demonstrated in this proof-of-concept study could be applied to other AI systems to decrease performance disparities and potentially improve model performance.

papers.title: Agentic Pipeline for Large-Scale Clinical Data Queries in Enterprise Electronic Health Records
papers.abstract: Using electronic health record (EHR) data to answer clinical research questions is challenging. It requires understanding the research question, finding relevant information across different sources, and combining that information to produce meaningful results. We developed an agentic large language model (LLM) pipeline that decomposes investigator-authored requests into source-specific tasks, generates and executes SQL on EHR, integrates structured and unstructured EHR evidence, and applies study-specific clinical note adjudication. We evaluated this workflow against data analyst-identified cohorts across 50 pediatric orthopedic clinical data query requests. Of these, 43 were included in manual-review-adjusted performance analyses. The median adjusted positive predictive value, sensitivity among patients identified by either approach, and corresponding F1 score were 0.93 (95% CI, 0.88-0.98), 0.92 (95% CI, 0.90-0.95) and 0.90 (95% CI, 0.87-0.94), respectively. These findings support the feasibility of translating natural-language research intent into executable, autonomous multi-stage EHR workflows.

papers.title: LLM Embeddings Complement Theory-Driven Language Features and Cognitive Scores for APOE4 and Aβ Prediction
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

papers.title: The LAMp-LC Study: Unveiling the lung microbiome in Australians with early- and late-stage lung cancer using shotgun metagenomics
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. Here, we characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n=106, healthy n=10) using shotgun metagenomics and semi-quantitative culture to evaluate site-specific microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across early- and late-stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culture-based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking pack-years, sex, and tumour characteristics. Cumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive core commensal depletion (Neisseria subflava, Gemella sanguinis, Rothia mucilaginosa), alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. {beta} diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst Shannon diversity ( diversity) was significantly reduced in early-stage compared with late-stage BWs. The early-stage TME also demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched (Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted (Streptococcus parasanguinis, Streptococcus cristatus, R. mucilaginosa) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only lung adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral {beta}-diversity restructuring. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiome-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST): Comparing Self-Triage Systems and Multiple Generations of OpenAI Models Against Preliminary Expert Consensus
papers.abstract: As digital self-triage becomes more widely used, quality assurance requires evaluation of both emergency recognition and overall agreement with clinical judgement, including how these outcomes differ across generations of large language models. The Benchmark Self-Triage (BeST) project intends to provide a framework to compare systems for digital self-triage against a medical 'gold standard' in Germany. As a first step in developing and demonstrating the methodology, we compared study-specific implementations of SmED 5.4.11 accessed via API and Infermedica Engine API via Microsoft Azure Healthcare Agent Service with five structured OpenAI configurations spanning multiple model generations: gpt-4.1, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol, and gpt-6-astra. The manufacturers of SmED and Infermedica offer MDR-certified Class IIb triage products, but these certified products were not directly evaluated. An LLM-based patient actor covered 480 physician-curated vignettes derived from German routine triage data. A pool of seven physicians provided preliminary reference classifications and consensus for 480 vignettes. Recommendations were mapped to three urgency categories-emergency, acute, and not urgent-and evaluated using winsorised weights derived from routine triage frequencies. Weighted emergency sensitivity ranged from 51.3% (95% CI 35.5-66.3%) for gpt-4.1 to 99.9% (99.7-100.0%) for gpt-6-astra. Weighted exact three-category agreement (accuracy) ranged from 54.4% to 68.8%; gpt-4.1 achieved the highest agreement despite the lowest emergency sensitivity. No system performed best across all urgency categories. The later-generation OpenAI configurations showed a more precautionary triage profile resembling SmED, with higher sensitivity for emergency cases; gpt-6-astra showed the strongest shift. This cross-sectional comparison across model generations suggests a shift towards more precautionary triage behaviour, without establishing a longitudinal improvement in accuracy. These findings highlight the limitations of overall agreement for evaluating self-triage and support category-specific assessment. Broader expert consensus and evaluation, as well as further steps to reduce dependence on SmED-derived source data, are needed and planned before drawing conclusions about clinical safety.

papers.title: Automating postmarketing pharmacovigilance with large language model agents
papers.abstract: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance relies on spontaneous adverse event reporting and labor-intensive observational studies, which suffer from underreporting and delayed risk detection. Large language model (LLM) agents could automate real-world evidence generation, but generalist agents make ad hoc analytical decisions that compromise epidemiological validity and reproducibility. Here we present MedCheckpoint, a multi-agent LLM system for automated postmarketing pharmacovigilance. MedCheckpoint grounds each analytical stage in a curated, source-traceable medical knowledge base, locks core study-design parameters before execution, performs patient-level analyses with human-written deterministic statistical tools, and enforces checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses, with optional human-in-the-loop review. We evaluated MedCheckpoint using a 54-question benchmark on a dual-purpose simulated electronic health record (EHR) testbed of 2.7 million individuals, designed with reliable clinical signals to evaluate routine analytical accuracy alongside spurious signals to stress-test system rigor. Across the benchmark, MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines in report quality across five dimensions rated by three independent LLM judges (overall means 4.81-4.88 versus 4.25-4.55 and 4.02-4.29) and yielded higher run-to-run consistency (mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440). Crucially, while baselines failed on up to 2 of 21 runs when handling infeasible comparisons or unmeasurable outcomes, MedCheckpoint produced no misleading failures across all seven stress-test trap questions with known data limitations. MedCheckpoint enables reliable, auditable, and scalable pharmacovigilance analysis.

papers.title: Nationwide Functional Profiling Enables Clinical Reclassification of KCNH2 Variants in the French LQT2 Population
papers.abstract: Background: The increasing use of genetic testing has identified thousands of KCNH2 variants associated with long QT syndrome type 2 (LQT2), yet most remain variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Translating functional abnormalities into clinically actionable evidence remains a major challenge. We established a nationwide functional genomics strategy to systematically characterize KCNH2 variants identified in the French LQT2 population and improve their clinical interpretation. Methods: We characterized 303 KCNH2 variants, including 201 VUS, using standardized high-throughput automated patch-clamp electrophysiology and complementary membrane trafficking assays. Nine electrophysiological parameters were integrated using MeTAL to predict variant-specific repolarization phenotypes under homozygous and heterozygous conditions. Modeled QTc values were compared with patient electrocardiographic data and variant-specific penetrance estimates. Functional evidence was calibrated against established benign and pathogenic variants using ClinGen-recommended categorical OddsPath and continuous likelihood-ratio approaches. Results: Multidimensional functional profiling revealed abnormalities not captured by current amplitude alone, identifying additional variants with clinically relevant repolarization defects. Among variants assessed under heterozygous conditions, MeTAL predictions showed 82.9% concordance with patient QTc phenotypes for ACMG class 5 variants, with apparent discordances partly consistent with incomplete penetrance. Continuous likelihood-ratio calibration demonstrated strong discrimination between established benign and pathogenic variants (AUC=0.936) and provided graded functional evidence for 76.1% of VUS. Integration of calibrated functional evidence into the ACMG/AMP framework enabled reclassification of 64 of 201 VUS (31.8%), including 7 as pathogenic, 46 as likely pathogenic, and 11 as likely benign. Conclusions: This nationwide study establishes a scalable framework integrating high-throughput electrophysiology, computational modeling, and clinical phenotyping to translate complex KCNH2 channel dysfunction into clinically interpretable evidence. The resulting reclassification of nearly one-third of VUS, together with the open-access HAMMER database, provides a resource to improve molecular diagnosis and risk assessment in LQT2.

papers.title: Expert-level localization of fine-grained cardiac structures across the transthoracic echocardiogram
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence models for echocardiography interpret studies without identifying the structures that support their outputs. We show that this spatial grounding does not emerge from the pretraining of current vision-language models. General-purpose and medical vision-language models and an open-vocabulary detector recalled 3% or fewer of cardiac structures and scored below a box that never sees the image. EchoLens, a detector trained on 5,912 expert-annotated structures and 4,219 Doppler signals from 136 patients, recalled 87% and localized structures as reliably as a blinded expert reader (box centre within the reference in 95.7% and 95.3% of cases). It covers 21 structures across 11 transthoracic views and 11 spectral Doppler signal types. In external data, two physicians judged 81-92% of its detections correct across all 11 views, and it identified the Doppler signal type in 83% of frames. EchoLens provides the spatial layer that grounded echocardiographic interpretation requires.

papers.title: Low-dose computed tomography and rapid molecular sputum testing in adults with suspected non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia: the HAP-FAST pilot sequential multiple assignment randomised trial with embedded qualitative and costing studies
papers.abstract: Background Non-ventilator-associated hospital-acquired pneumonia (nv-HAP) diagnosis is imprecise; chest x-rays (CXR) lack detail and sputum culture delays targeted prescribing. However, the evidence base to support diagnostic improvement is sparse. We assessed the feasibility of a trial of low-dose thoracic CT and rapid molecular testing of sputum. Methods HAP-FAST was a UK NIHR funded, open-label pilot sequential multiple assignment randomised trial with qualitative and costing substudies in four UK hospitals (ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT05483309). Using research without prior consent (RWPC) and site-stratified web-based randomisation, clinicians allocated adults with suspected nv-HAP (excluding pregnancy and palliation), before their second antibiotic dose, 1:1 to CT or CXR; participants subsequently treated for nv-HAP with sputum available underwent another 1:1 randomisation to BIOFIRE(R) FILMARRAY(R) Pneumonia plus Panel (FAPP) with standard microbiology or standard microbiology alone . Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, consent, intervention delivery and data completeness through 90 days. Adverse events were not systematically collected. Analyses were intention-to-treat and descriptive. Results Between June 2023 and March 2024, 220 adults were randomised at stage-1 (109 CT; 111 CXR), reaching target three months early. Of 154/220 (70.0%) subsequently managed as nv-HAP, 92/154 (59.7%) could not produce sputum. 62/154 (40.3%; 28.2% of stage-1) were randomised to stage-2: 31 FAPP and 31 no-FAPP. Allocated imaging was recorded for 75/109 (68.8%) CT and 99/111 (89.2%) CXR participants; 6/31(19.4%) FAPP tests were not completed. Consent for follow-up was obtained for 142/220 (64.5%). Protocol-defined clinical cure was assessable in 1/220 participants. The day-90 resource-use questionnaire was returned by 55/110 participants (50.0%). Qualitative findings supported RWPC but identified needs for staged communication, lower-burden follow-up and improved diagnostic pathways. Excess bed days and readmissions drove costs but data capture requires refinement. Conclusions A definitive trial is plausible only with enhanced RWPC, diagnostic delivery and follow-up pathways, improved sputum procedures, stewardship-aligned outcomes and routine economic data capture.

papers.title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, noninvasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-beta burden using Cookie Theft picture descriptions from two cohorts of Hebrew- and English-speaking participants (IRAP, N=134; WRAP, N=1,541). Amyloid-beta burden was classified using lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) with standard cognitive test scores, reflecting conventional clinical assessment, and theory-driven linguistic features, reflecting traditional language analysis. Embedding-based models achieved the highest F1 scores among constituent models in five of eight tasks involving APOE4 status and global amyloid-beta burden. High prediction disagreement suggested complementary signals across approaches. An any-positive ensemble significantly outperformed every constituent model and a prior-informed random baseline across all eight tasks, and significantly outperformed all constituent models in 21 of 24 regional amyloid-beta tasks. These findings highlight the complementarity of LLM-based, theory-driven, and cognitive measures for predicting AD-related genetic risk and amyloid pathology, and support further investigation of their potential for early screening approaches.

papers.title: MENTOR: An Evidence-Informed Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Efficient Selection of Institution-Specific Negative Control Outcomes
papers.abstract: Objective Negative control outcomes (NCOs) help detect and correct systematic error in observational studies, yet their selection remains largely manual. The Common Evidence Model (CEM) can generate candidate lists, but researchers must still screen them for plausibility as true nulls and for sufficient observation in each institution's data. We developed and evaluated MENTOR (Multi-agent Evidence-informed Negative conTrol Outcome selection with Reasoning), a multi-agent system of large language models (LLMs) that combines CEM evidence with LLM reasoning to select institution-specific NCOs. Methods Four LLM agents operate on an institution's Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership common data model. A Curator summarizes drug labels, a Suggester assesses locally frequent candidates with CEM evidence and a first-pass LLM judgment, an Adjudicator resolves their disagreements, and a Diagnostician relaxes the patient-count threshold until a target number of NCOs is met. Using Qwen3.6-27B, we evaluated 349 candidates for three drug pairs in a Korean tertiary hospital's electronic health records (2.9 million patients) against a blinded LLM judge from a different model family, validated by three experts on 90 candidates. We compared accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), and sensitivity with CEM-only and first-pass-LLM-only selection. Results MENTOR proposed 243 NCOs versus 121 by CEM-only, with higher accuracy (0.83 [0.79-0.87] vs. 0.53 [0.48-0.58]), sensitivity (0.89 vs. 0.41), and PPV (0.86 vs. 0.79). Judge-expert agreement was {kappa}=0.63. Adjudication, needed for 44.1% of candidates, added little accuracy, and only with reasoning mode. Concordant acceptances, which bypass it, contained about half of the false positives. Only 7%-9% of CEM-proposed outcomes had at least 10,000 patients at the institution. Conclusion Combining LLM judgments with CEM evidence and local data yielded more NCOs, with higher PPV, than CEM alone. Restricting reasoning to discordant candidates kept computation time below 40% of that with reasoning in all agents. Every decision comes with its evidence and rationale for investigators' final review.

papers.title: Trait-Level Rather Than Individual-Level Resolution in Fitness Genomics: A Population-Calibrated Variant Prioritization Framework in a South Asian Cohort
papers.abstract: Translating candidate gene panels into objective physiological trait interpretations remains a major hurdle in exercise genomics. Conventional total genotype scoring suffers from severe panel-composition bias, fails to evaluate unannotated or novel variants, and frequently fosters inflated claims regarding individual athletic prediction. Here, we present a population-calibrated, multi-tiered computational framework that evaluates genomic variation across six evidence streams integrating deep learning protein and genomic language models (ESM-2, Evo 2), missense and splice predictors (AlphaMissense, SpliceAI), and regional pathogenic-density metrics to generate a continuous Variant Priority Score (VPS; 1-10 scale). By dynamically renormalizing missing evidence streams rather than zero-filling them, the framework robustly scores unannotated variants lacking empirical database entries. Individual trait burden across 344 genes (spanning 17 physiological traits in Aerobic, Anaerobic, and Recovery domains) is aggregated and normalized against ancestry-matched expectations derived from gnomAD South Asian and an in-house reference cohort (N > 13,000). When applied to 960 South Indian individuals (584 male, 376 female; whole-exome sequencing), this normalization removed the dependence of expected trait burden on panel size by construction, and gene count explained only 2.7% of the variance in the resulting capacity scores (six traits interrogated by 16 to 33 genes). Variance partitioning of 4,764 individual-by-trait scores (six of the 17 traits: one aerobic, two anaerobic and three recovery) revealed that score variation was predominantly trait-driven (45.5%) rather than individual-driven (11.1%, p = 0.386), a pattern reproduced independently in males and females and with no statistically significant gender difference in capacity scores, indicating that, in this cohort, the candidate panel resolved differences between physiological traits but did not detect differences between individuals in capacity scores (no athletic phenotype was measured). Benchmarking against ClinVar classifications achieved an AUC of 0.74, which fell to 0.62 when archive-dependent streams were excluded, directly quantifying the role of shared data provenance. Replacing the in-house frequency reference with gnomAD South Asian shifted absolute scores (median fold change 0.73) but preserved trait ordering (Spearman 0.96), so scores are positions against a stated, population-specific reference. This framework provides an auditable, evidence-traceable baseline for trait-level research and functional variant prioritization while offering a critical methodological safeguard against over-interpreting unvalidated individual performance predictions.
